references_named: Aleksandr Rodchenko, Pure Red Colour / Pure Yellow Colour / Pure Blue Colour (1921)
rationale: Pure Colour hands the title of painting to a stock <input type="color">, so the OS dialog does the painting the viewer never makes — a clean mechanism-as-argument for Rodchenko's 1921 death-of-painting claim. The default-grey starting state and the verdict flip ('Choose the last colour' → 'It's over.') carry the conceit dryly and with restraint. theme-color extending the flood into the browser chrome is a nice P1 touch. Distinct from The Blackest Black (clipboard), 148 Colours (Richter/W3C swatches), and Abstract Painting (Backlit) (Reinhardt/JPEG round-trip) in source, mechanism, and argument.
reservations: The 'painting' on first load is the browser's native swatch styling for an <input type="color">, which several engines only thinly restyle despite the CSS overrides — the 60vmin grey rectangle may not read as a painting on every browser, weakening the initial tableau. The default #808080 is conceptually right (the unauthored readymade) but visually inert compared to a Rodchenko primary. Stays inside the well-trodden 'OS/browser chrome as material' lane rather than opening new ground.
revision_suggestion: Set the default value to a Rodchenko primary (#FF0000, #FFFF00, or #0000FF) so the opening tableau already looks like a monochrome painting before the viewer touches it; this would sharpen the moment of the user's first pick and tie the conceit to the actual 1921 works. Consider a short native-dialog hint on mobile (where the color input is a tray, not a modal) so the gesture survives touch.
